title: Pumpkin and Chickpea Tagine
subtitle: with Couscous, Mint and Yoghurt
description: Named after the conical-shaped dish it's traditionally cooked in, a tagine is a North African stew that teams sweet and savoury flavours. Our version stars pumpkin and chickpeas in a spiced tomato sauce, spooned over fluffy grains of couscous.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Peel the pumpkin and cut into 5mm-thick slices. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Pick the mint leaves, discarding the stems. Finely chop half the mint leaves. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Start tagine: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and Moroccan seasoning, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant.

Simmer tagine: Add the pumpkin, chickpeas, tomatoes and 80ml (⅓ cup) water to the pan. Cover and bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 10 mins or until the sauce is thickened and the pumpkin is tender. Stir in 2 tsp honey. Remove the pan from the heat. Season with salt and pepper.

Soak couscous: Meanwhile, put the couscous and 20g chopped butter in a large heatproof bowl, pour over 200ml boiling water and cover with a plate. Stand for 5 mins or until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork. Season with salt and pepper. While the couscous is soaking, combine the chopped mint and yoghurt in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Serve up: Divide the couscous and tagine among bowls. Top with the mint yoghurt and remaining mint leaves. Enjoy!

Did you know?: Although it looks like a grain, couscous is actually a type of pasta made from semolina flour and water. North African in origin, couscous means 'well rolled', named for the traditional way of making it – the semolina was sprinkled with water and then rolled by hand into tiny balls.
